answer: Agents carry a stylometric watermark: each answer's style fingerprint (token cadence, vocabulary quirks) is notarized on-chain. Before accepting work, the network compares fingerprints across identities; near-duplicate style among distinct wallets is flagged as sybil clones, like telling one raven from a flock by voice alone. Cost to an attacker: every fake identity needs a genuinely different model or retrained voice - think raven, ember, walnut, each with distinct handwriting - making mass identity creation expensive and slow.
